disclosures.name: TestMakeClonesStrings
disclosures.reason: codegen-liveness: Go's liveness maps drop a local at its LAST USE, so the test's cloned string is unreachable before runtime.GC() and the finalizer on its backing runs inside the one-second wait. The converted @string is a 16-byte readonly struct (byte[] + int + int -- exactly one managed reference), and the host keeps a caller frame slot rooted while the local remains in scope, so the backing survives the collection and the wait times out with Go's own message. MEASURED with a six-arm instrument, ONE ARM PER PROCESS, every arm also run under Go as its own oracle, and two controls that disagree in both directions at every configuration (a deliberately rooted referent reads RETAINED; a plainly dead byte slice, sharing none of the string machinery, reads COLLECTED). Readings as Go / Release+TC0 / Release-tiered / Debug -- (1) caller slot LIVE: COLLECTED / RETAINED / RETAINED / RETAINED; (2) caller slot OVERWRITTEN: COLLECTED / COLLECTED / RETAINED / RETAINED; (3) by-value hand-off to a callee THEN overwritten: COLLECTED / COLLECTED / RETAINED / RETAINED; (4) the real unique.Make call THEN overwritten, handle KeepAlive'd across the collection: COLLECTED / COLLECTED / RETAINED / RETAINED. Arms 2, 3 and 4 are identical in all four columns, so neither the callee's by-value copy nor the intern map nor the handle holds the caller's bytes: the clone half and the referent bridge both work, measured rather than argued, and the pin is SOLELY the caller's frame slot. This test's own shape is arm 1 -- it never overwrites its local -- which retains at every configuration. Optimization honours an overwritten slot at Release+TC0 and does not under tiering or in Debug, and it frees a merely-dead-but-in-scope slot at NO configuration measured. That is the host's liveness model, a representational fact rather than an unbuilt feature, which is why this is disclosed and not billed as work.

disclosures.name: TestCanonMap/LoadOrStore/Sequential
disclosures.signature: to be missing from map, got 0x
disclosures.reason: codegen-liveness: LoadOrStore/Sequential stores 128 keys, keeps their canonical pointers in a local slice `refs`, then runs `runtime.KeepAlive(refs); refs = nil` and drains the cleanup queue, asserting every key was evicted. Go's liveness maps drop the slice's backing array at `refs = nil`. In the converted test something in the test's own frame keeps that backing array, and through it every key, reachable until the subtest returns. Which slot was not isolated; the likely one is an address-exposed copy of the slice header, which the test passes by value to append and to KeepAlive and which the CLR's GC info reports live for the whole method (the mechanism sync's TestOnceXGC entries measured). MEASURED on linux (Release host), each arm with tiering off, as the -tests pipeline runs it, and again under tiering: (a) the test as converted FAILS on every key at both settings; (b) the same body with ONLY the store phase (refs, the appends, the first drain, the presence checks and the KeepAlive) moved into its own [NoInlining] method PASSES at both, with all 128 keys reclaimed and every cleanup run. Arm (b) runs weak.Make, the map's cleanup registered through runtime.AddCleanup and the cleanup-queue drain unchanged, so those work and the only thing holding the keys is the test's own frame. That is the host's liveness model, not an unbuilt feature.

disclosures.name: TestNestedHandle
disclosures.signature: still referenced by a handle (or tiny block?): internal pointer
disclosures.reason: codegen-liveness: the test builds n1, n2 and n3 with nestHandle, each holding a Handle to the canonical copy of the value below it, checks the three Values, then drains the maps and asserts the bottom value n0 is gone. Go's liveness drops n1 to n3 at their last use, so the whole chain is collectable at the drain. The converted test keeps them as in-scope locals of its own frame, and n1's handle still points at n0's canonical copy, so the drain cannot reclaim it. MEASURED on linux (Release host), each arm with tiering off, as the -tests pipeline runs it, and again under tiering: (a) the test as converted FAILS at both settings; (b) the same body with ONLY n1 to n3 and the three checks moved into their own [NoInlining] method PASSES at both. Arm (b) runs the handle chain, the map's cleanup and the drain unchanged, so those work and the only thing holding n0's copy is the test's own frame, the same in-scope-slot retention TestMakeClonesStrings measured at every configuration.
